haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any store call. Redis is not touched, so no counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: Limited to one shared budget per customer, so the plan limit applies in total: 100 per minute for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: 429 with Retry-After in seconds, X-RateLimit-Limit, and X-RateLimit-Remaining 0. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. The check runs before the increment, and a rejected request increments nothing.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. An allowed request is counted before forwarding, so a backend 500 still uses budget.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded unchanged, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and no X-RateLimit headers are sent. Never 429 or 5xx.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise has no number yet (OPEN), so no limit is enforced and no headers are sent.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, one key per customer per minute, rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. A 120-second TTL removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: Each new one-minute window uses a new key starting at zero. Old keys expire after their 120-second TTL.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script on one key, so Redis serializes requests and the count cannot pass the limit.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds until the current window ends, rounded up, minimum 1. Since windows are one minute, the value is 1 to 60.
haiku-low.q12: Retries are NOT STATED. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, since no count is known.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized, and Redis is not touched, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: The budget is per customer, not per key, so all three keys share one budget: the plan limit per minute in total (Standard 100 per minute).
sonnet.q3: A 429 with Retry-After (seconds), X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The backend never sees the rejected request.
sonnet.q4: No. The check runs before the increment and a rejected request increments nothing.
sonnet.q5: Yes. An allowed request is counted before forwarding, so a backend 500 still uses budget.
sonnet.q6: It fails open. The gateway forwards the request unchanged to the backend, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and sends no X-RateLimit headers. It never returns 429 or 5xx because of a store error.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is not decided (OPEN, a Product decision), so no limit is enforced for now.
sonnet.q8: In shared Redis, in one key per customer per minute, rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Old counts are removed by a 120-second TTL on the key.
sonnet.q9: When the fixed one-minute window rolls over. The next window uses a new key, aligned to the Redis clock, so the count starts again at zero.
sonnet.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script on a single Redis key. Redis serializes requests from different instances, so the count can never pass the limit.
sonnet.q11: It is the seconds until the current window ends, rounded up, with a minimum of 1, so always 1 to 60. The script computes it from Redis TIME.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. The document says it forwards the request (fail open) after the 50 ms timeout or error, and the client gets no X-RateLimit headers.
